sentences.text:
This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants,
namely the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, taking exception to the impugned award dated 12.12.2009 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia (M.P.) in Claim Case No.
68/2009, whereby the Claims Tribunal exonerated the respondent-Insurance Company from its liability to pay compensation and fastened the liability upon the appellants/owner and driver of the vehicle.
2. The date of the accident and the issue of negligence are not in dispute between the parties.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality and are not under challenge in the present appeal.
The only dispute involved in this appeal relates to the fixation of liability to pay compensation.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:427 2 MA-108-2010 deceased- Jayendra Singh Yadav due to a motor accident,
compensation to the tune of Rs.8,25,500/- along with interest has been awarded in favour of the claimants.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal is contrary to the settled principles of law.

It is contended that the Tribunal has gravely Om Prakash Sharma vs Smt.Bhooridevi on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160293219/
1 erred in fixing the liability upon the appellants despite the admitted position that the offending vehicle was comprehensively insured at the time of the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that appellant No. 1 was neither in possession nor in control of the vehicle on the date of the accident and, therefore, no liability could have been fastened upon the appellants.
According to the appellants, the vehicle was admittedly in possession of the concerned Bank under a hire purchase agreement at the relevant time.

Learned counsel placed reliance upon the evidence of PW-3, the General Manager of the Bank, who deposed that the vehicle in question was released on 20.04.2009, whereas the accident occurred on 22.04.2009.
It was argued that, therefore, the vehicle was not in possession of the Bank at the time of the accident.
It was also submitted that PW-2, the Branch Manager, supported the version of the appellants.
On these grounds, prayer was made for setting aside the impugned award and for fastening the liability upon the Insurance Company to pay compensation to the claimants.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:427 3 MA-108-2010 of the Claims Tribunal.
7.

On perusal of Ex. D-5, it is evident that the said document is an agreement between Jila Sahakari Krishi Evam Gramin Vikas Bank Maryadit, Datia and the owner of the offending vehicle, whereby the vehicle was given on hire purchase to the Bank for the period from 01.02.2009 to 31.07.2009.

entities.text: Jila Sahakari Krishi Evam Gramin Vikas Bank Maryadit
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The accident occurred on 22.04.2009.
The execution and validity of this agreement were not disputed by the appellants.
It is also undisputed that the offending vehicle was insured for private use and not for commercial purpose.
8. The moot question involved in the present appeal is whether, at the time of the accident on 22.04.2009, the offending vehicle was in possession of the Bank or in possession of the owner.

9. In view of the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellants, it is evident that though it was contended that an application dated 20.04.2009 was filed before the Manager, Jila Sahakari Krishi Evam Gramin Vikas Bank, Datia seeking return of the jeep into the possession of the owner, the said application was admittedly received by a person who was neither examined before the Claims Tribunal nor subjected to cross- examination.

entities.text: Jila Sahakari Krishi Evam Gramin Vikas Bank
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said person was the best witness to prove that the application was received by him and that possession of the offending vehicle was delivered to the owner on 20.04.2009.
In the absence of such evidence, an adverse presumption is liable to be drawn against the appellants.

10. According to Ex. D-5, it is clearly established that at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was in possession of the Bank under a hire NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:427 4 MA-108-2010 purchase arrangement, and the vehicle was given on rent,
whereas the insurance policy covered only private use and not commercial purpose.

Om Prakash Sharma vs Smt.Bhooridevi on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160293219/
2 11.

Although PW-2 and PW-3 deposed that at the time of the accident the offending vehicle was not in possession of the Bank, their evidence does not inspire confidence, as the person who received the application Ex. P-10 was not examined before the Claims Tribunal.
Moreover, Ex. P-10 is only a photocopy and was not duly proved.
It was the duty of the appellants to summon the relevant record from the Bank to establish that the vehicle was actually returned to them on 20.04.2009, which they failed to do.
12. In the absence of the aforesaid evidence, it could not be proved by the appellants that at the time of the accident the offending vehicle was not in possession of the Bank.
13. The learned Claims Tribunal, in paragraphs 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22 of the impugned award, has elaborately discussed every aspect of the matter.
This Court finds no reason to interfere with the well-reasoned findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal are correct in the eye of law.
14. Consequently, the appeal filed by the appellants is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
